title: Incidence of metabolic acidosis following continued administration of SGLT2 inhibitors in cardiac surgery patients
summary: SGLT2 inhibitors are medications used to treat type 2 diabetes and heart failure. During surgery, however, they may promote the buildup of substances called ketone bodies, which can make the blood too acidic. This complication can occur even when blood sugar levels are nearly normal and may therefore initially go unnoticed. This study investigates how levels of the ketone body β-hydroxybutyrate change around the time of heart surgery in patients taking SGLT2 inhibitors.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Written informed consent obtained after the patient has received information about the study
• Age ≥18 years
• Scheduled elective cardiac surgery or elective transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI)
• Pre-existing treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors, initiated at least 7 days before the scheduled procedure and continued until the day of the procedure
Exclusion criteria:
• Age <18 years
• Emergency procedures
• Absence of, or inability to provide, written informed consent to participate in the study
• Patients who initiated SGLT2 inhibitor therapy ≤7 days before the day of surgery
